format.scenarios: Each scenario starts fresh hosts, runs its steps with a pause after each for in-memory traffic to settle, then closes the clients, the server and the workers in that order. `frames` lists every frame sent, in the order sent, with its link and the side that sent it. Within one link and direction the order is the protocol's; across links it is this run's.
format.links: `client` and `client2` are WebSocket links (an in-memory WebSocket pair: one text message per frame) between a client host and the server, accepted as acceptWebSockets accepts them. `worker` is an in-memory link between the server and the worker its `session:` route spawned. `raw` links are bare peers the fixture drives by hand.
format.omitted: `ack` frames are not recorded: when they are sent depends on timer order. The flow scenarios hold the client's acknowledgements back; `gate` records the one they release.
format.normalized: Root ids carry a random incarnation, replaced by `*` (`server#*:3`). Compare ping and pong `n` and error messages as placeholders.
format.contracts: The contract descriptions the scenarios use, after a JSON round trip.

scenarios.name: hello
scenarios.description: A client connects and leaves: both hellos, then the client's bye.

scenarios.name: hold
scenarios.description: A guest holds a counter (shape, variant viewer); holds that fail are gone: forbidden by the factory, an unknown type, a contract that is not covered and one of another version (upgrade_required for a client), and an invalid input. Then it releases the live hold.

error.message: unavailable/unknown_type: noel.test.missing is not served by server
upgrade_required: contract_mismatch: noel.test.counter@1 does not cover the consumer's description (owner.add result); forgotten version bump?
upgrade_required: contract_mismatch: noel.test.counter: provider version 1, consumer version 2, no accepts adapter

scenarios.name: state
scenarios.description: An owner subscribes to a counter: snapshot, then ops through one delta encoder (an inline path, then a definition and references, an `r` that clears them), unsubscribes, subscribes again for a new snapshot, and releases.

scenarios.name: call
scenarios.description: Calls with a result, a void result, invalid arguments (invalid/args) and a method that throws (unavailable).

error.message: invalid/args: noel.test.counter�{"name":"a"}�host.add args: / must be integer

scenarios.name: cancel
scenarios.description: With maxCalls 1, a waiting call is cancelled by the caller (aborted), a second call meanwhile is refused at once (unavailable/too_many_calls), and releasing a subscribed hold sends unsub then release.

error.message: unavailable/too_many_calls: Too many calls in progress on this connection (1); wait for earlier ones to finish

scenarios.name: relay
scenarios.description: An owner holds a session object on a worker through the server's route: the server stamps the principal on the relayed hold, forwards the subscription, calls (with a root, ended by root_end) and a cancel, then the release.

scenarios.name: refused
scenarios.description: A guest of session s1: its hold on s2 is refused by the route (forbidden), a host without a route is unavailable, and a principal it forges in its hold is ignored: the worker sees the stamped guest.

error.message: forbidden: session:s2 refused for this principal

scenarios.name: invalidate
scenarios.description: invalidatePrincipal({kind: guest, id: g1}) on the server: a link accepted with restamp keeps its link under revision 2 and holds again; one without is closed. Relays under the old principal are gone, released downstream, and the pattern propagates to the worker.

scenarios.name: ping
scenarios.description: Both sides ping every 100 ms and answer pings with pongs; the run lasts 150 ms.

scenarios.name: ping-timeout
scenarios.description: A peer that says hello and then nothing: pings every 100 ms, and after 250 ms without a frame the link closes with `ping timeout`.

scenarios.name: flow-coalesce
scenarios.description: Window 200: while the client holds back its acknowledgements, state waits once the window is full while results go out; the released ack sends the waiting ops as one frame.

scenarios.name: flow-reset
scenarios.description: Window 64: a waiting subscription whose ops outgrow four windows is replaced by a reset of the current value; the released ack sends the reset and the ops after it.

scenarios.name: version-old-peer
scenarios.description: A peer whose hello has no protocol (version 1): the server answers with its hello, then closes with `protocol-version 2`.

scenarios.name: version-new-server
scenarios.description: A client whose server says protocol 3: the client closes with `protocol-version 2`.

scenarios.name: violations
scenarios.description: Protocol violations close the link: a malformed frame, a duplicate hold id, a control frame from a child, a hello that does not match how the peer was accepted, and an ack outside the expected range.
